newsitem.title: USA: Snoop Doggy Dogg album leaps to top of U.S. charts.
newsitem.headline: Snoop Doggy Dogg album leaps to top of U.S. charts.

text.p: The new album by gangsta rapper Snoop Doggy Dogg opened at the top of the U.S. album charts with first week sales down 40 percent from those for his previous release, according to data released by his record company on Wednesday.
"Tha Doggfather," sold almost 479,000 copies in the week ended November 17, giving it a comfortable lead over last week's number one from Dogg's deceased label-mate, Tupac Shakur.

However Dogg's solo debut, "Doggystyle," sold 803,000 copies during its first week in December 1993, when he was at the center of a murder probe that led to his acquittal by a Los Angeles jury earlier this year. Dogg, whose real name is Calvin Broadus, was featured prominently on the soundtrack to "Murder Was The Case," which sold 329,000 copies in its first week in October 1994.

He records for Death Row Records, which claimed the number two position with Shakur's "The Don Killuminati -- The 7 Day Theory," recorded under his alter ego, Makaveli. Shakur was killed in an unsolved drive-by shooting in Las Vegas in September. In the latest week, his album sold almost 250,000 copies, giving it a two-week total of more than 1.1 million, Death Row said.
Death Row is owned by businessman Suge Knight, who is currently in jail on possible parole violations. He faces a prison term of up to nine years.

The latest sales data are good news for Seagram Co Ltd's MCA Music Entertainment, which distributes the first three albums through its Interscope Records affiliate. Interscope handles southern California modern rock group No Doubt, whose "Tragic Kingdom" rose a notch to third with sales of over 139,000.

Sony Corp grabbed the next two positions as Canadian singer Celine Dion's "Falling Into You," slipped one place to fourth and the rap compilation, "Mo Thugs Family Scriptures," dropped to fifth after debuting in second last week.

Dion records for Sony's Epic Records label, while the Mo Thugs compilation is distributed by Sony's Relativity Records under a deal with the nascent Mo Thugs Records label owned by members of Bone Thugs-N-Harmony.

New releases this week had a heavy theatrical bent. Opening in sixth was Warner Bros.' soundtrack to Madonna's upcoming film, "Evita." Atlantic Records' soundtrack for the current number one movie, "Space Jam," was 13th, followed in 16th by the soundtrack for Barbra Streisand's "The Mirror Has Two Faces," which was third at the weekend box office.
Warner Bros. Records and Atlantic are units of Time Warner Inc. The "Mirror" album is released by Sony's Columbia Records.
